newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan tells Knesset team it wants peace progress.
newsitem.headline: Jordan tells Knesset team it wants peace progress.

text.p: Jordanian leaders on Thursday told prominent Israeli Knesset members visiting Amman that progress in Israeli-Palestinian peace talks was essential for Middle East peace, officials said.

Yossi Beilin, head of a Labour Party delegation among the 17 strong parliamentary group, told reporters after talks with Crown Prince Hassan and Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti they reviewed Israeli-Palestinian ties, final status talks on a permanent settlement and the thorny issue of the status of Jerusalem.
The delegation also included an all-party nine-member delegation from the Knesset's economic committee, Israeli embassy spokesman Shalom Tourgman told Reuters earlier.
"We shared the view that eventually an agreement will be signed on Hebron and it will open the way for further talks and further deployments," said Beilin.
Beilin, a leading Labour party member, voicing "cautious optimism about the future" despite current snags over a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.

In Jerusalem, a top aide to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday accused the PLO of stalling in the talks on Hebron but Palestinians said Israel's refusal to set dates for future redeployments was holding up an agreement.

Asked about Jordanian worries over current Israeli policies, Beilin said:"Jordan is a friend that is very concerned..it wants to see progress on the Israeli-Palestinian peace track...that without this progress it will be very very difficult to have further developments in Middle East peace."

Jordan's official ties with Israel have recently been strained by worries over the Jewish state's policy of strengthening settlements in the West Bank, which Amman views as a direct threat to its security.

Amman also fears the collapse of the peace process could spark renewed violence in Palestinian areas that will reverberate in Jordan, where a large portion of the population are of Palestinian origin.
The Knesset's economic team were separately briefed by senior economic officials on obstacles hindering business ties and means of overcoming them, officials said.

Crown Prince Hassan stressed the importance of trilateral Israeli-Palestinian-Jordanian economic cooperation to cement peace while the Knesset's economic committee pledged to lobby for dismantling barriers to expanded business links with Jordan, officials said.
